verdict: This is the bucket Skydo already wins. Skydo vs Payoneer, vs PayPal and vs Stripe are each cited 1.5 to 1.9 times per fetch; Xflow's comparisons of Skydo are fetched more and cited less than half as often. ChatGPT lifts the row labels of Skydo's comparison table and the 'X is better for / Skydo is better for' bullets almost verbatim. The one weak page, Skydo vs Wise at 0.61, loses share to Xflow's blog and to Wise's own pages, not to a better structure.

diagnosis: A two-brand comparison is answered as a table plus two 'choose X if' lists. Skydo's page is built as exactly that, so each block maps to a block in the answer.
Row labels are the citation unit. ChatGPT copies the left column of the table (fee structure, FX markup, FIRA, settlement, support, founded) and fills the cells from the page.
Honest two-sided bullets get cited. 'Payoneer is better for Upwork payouts' is quoted because it is true and specific; a page that only praises itself gives ChatGPT nothing for the other side.
Third-brand injection lowers the rate. Xflow's Skydo vs Wise page has three sections on Xflow that ChatGPT never quotes; they add fetch weight without citations.
Worked examples at several invoice sizes are copied whole. Infinity's page with three examples is cited 1.21 per fetch and ChatGPT reproduced every number.
Skydo's table headers are logos, so the crawled header reads '| Features | | |'. It still works on a two-column page because the H1 names the order, but it is fragile.
No date, no author on Skydo's compare template. 'As of January 2026' inside the text carries the recency for now.
Skydo vs Wise underperforms (0.61) because that query has more competition (Wise's own pages, Xflow's blog), not because the page differs from Skydo vs Payoneer.
spec: Keep the Skydo compare template. Replace logo header cells with text: Feature / Payoneer / Skydo.
Add a visible published and updated date, an author with title, and BlogPosting + Person schema alongside FAQPage.
Add a cost-at-three-sizes table: $1,000 / $5,000 / $20,000 with total cost and INR received for both brands, dated 'as of <month> 2026'.
Keep 'X is better for / Skydo is better for' at five bullets each and keep the competitor's real strengths.
Cut CTAs from 16 to four: hero, after the table, after the verdict, footer.

For Skydo vs Wise: add the Wise-specific facts ChatGPT wants (entity restriction to sole proprietors and freelancers, $10,000 per-transaction cap, $2.50 FIRA, April 2026 personal-account change) as table rows with dates.

playbook.use_when: The query names two brands: 'Skydo vs Wise', 'Payoneer vs Skydo for freelancers', 'Infinity payments vs Skydo fees'. ChatGPT answers with one table, two 'choose X if' lists and a cost example.
blueprint: H1 as the query with the year: '<Brand> vs Skydo: which is better for Indian exporters in 2026?'. Date, author and title under it.
Four-bullet summary of the differences with numbers (fee model, FX markup, FIRA, settlement).
One comparison table with text headers, 10-12 labelled rows grouped under Pricing, Compliance, Payment & experience. Every cell a fact with a number or a date.
Pricing section: the competitor's fee layers named one by one, then Skydo's flat fee. One worked example in prose.
Cost-at-three-sizes table ($1,000 / $5,000 / $20,000): total cost and INR received for both, dated.
Compliance and rails: paired statements, competitor first, Skydo second, for FIRA timing, eBRC, GST invoicing, purpose code, SOFTEX.
'<Brand> is better for' 5 bullets and 'Skydo is better for' 5 bullets. Keep the competitor's true strengths.
Two or three customer quotes with numbers, then 'How to migrate' in 5 timed steps with a documents list.
FAQ of 6-7 questions with two- to four-sentence factual answers that include the numbers.
1,300-1,700 words. Only two brands on the page. Four CTAs at most. No calculator-only content; keep the numbers in text.
